impact_scope.description: Replaces the byte-at-a-time CRC64 ECMA update implementation with an eight-byte slicing algorithm plus a one-byte remainder path, and expands the private lookup table from 1 to 8 rows. Public entries, arguments, state protocol, configuration, and input semantics are unchanged.

gap_before.type: CRC64 API not exposed by H0
evidence: In S0, ecma_hasher.update! already accepts a caller-supplied byte slice, mutates the hasher state, and is also reached through update_u64!.
H0 enables only AUX/BASE/JSON modules and exercises JSON decoding; it neither enables the CRC64 module nor constructs or calls ecma_hasher.

gap_after.type: CRC64 API not exposed by H0
evidence: In S1, the same ecma_hasher.update! and update_u64! public interfaces remain, with the same byte-slice input and state/checksum behavior at the caller boundary.
H0 remains limited to AUX/BASE/JSON and still neither enables CRC64 nor calls its hasher APIs; the new eight-byte and remainder paths are therefore unexercised for the same pre-existing reason.

new_harness_obligation.description: The commit adds no public entry, argument, buffer, call-order transition, configuration action, compile-time enablement, or new input construction requirement. Exercising CRC64 still requires the same module enablement, hasher construction, and byte-slice update call already required in S0.
evidence: The signatures of ecma_hasher.update!, update_u64!, and checksum_u64 are unchanged.
The eight-byte slicing loop and enlarged ECMA_TABLE are private implementation details selected automatically by the existing input length.

reason: For the stable scope of CRC64 ECMA hashing, H0 omits the subsystem in both S0 and S1. S1 changes only the internal algorithm and private table, without adding caller-facing exposure or control requirements. Thus the same material gap exists before and after, so the delta is UNCHANGED and the fixed rule yields no maintenance need.
